## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

Social meta-tag generator covering Open Graph and Twitter cards. /workspace/metagen: src/meta.js exports renderMeta({title, description, url, image, siteName, type}) producing the standard og pairs, twitter card summary_large_image when image exists else summary, a canonical link, and a plain title element plus meta description; description truncates at 155 characters on a word boundary with no dangling comma or space; all attribute values escaped. Also export parseMeta(html) using cheerio that inverts it back to an object, and test round-trip equality for canonical inputs. Vitest: round-trip, the truncation boundary with a 200-char description asserting length and no mid-word cut, escaping with quotes in the title, and card-type switching. Green suite via npx vitest run.

Two test issues:

1. Round-trip minimal: renderMeta defaults og:type to "website", so parseMeta returns type. The spec says "test round-trip equality for canonical inputs" — canonical input includes type: 'website' or we accept default. Simplest: include `type` in the minimal input, or treat the default as part of the object. I'll add `type: 'website'` to minimal input? Better: make parseMeta only meaningful for canonical inputs — but the default injection is real behavior. I'll just include type in the minimal test (canonical = fully specified). Or drop the og:type fallback in parseMeta when it equals default? No — keep behavior honest; fix test to expect type 'website'. Actually cleaner: minimal input gets `type: undefined` → output has type website. Canonical inputs should specify type. Update test.

2. Word-building loop produced 197 chars. Fix by padding with a filler word of exact length: after building ≤200, append spaces + filler. Simpler: construct deterministically: take words and pad final word with extra letters? That would break "word boundary" check? No—only boundary at cut point matters. Easiest: build desc then if length <200, extend last word by repeating a letter... changes word content but fine. Or choose different word list. Simplest robust: build from words while length < 200 - (wordlen+1)... Let me just do: start with base sentence, then pad with "filler" words until >=195, then append a final word padded with 'x' to reach exactly 200 without trailing space.

All green — 10/10 passing. Summary:

**`/workspace/metagen/src/meta.js`**
- `renderMeta({title, description, url, image, siteName, type})` emits:
  - `<title>` + `<meta name="description">`
  - `<link rel="canonical">` when `url` is set
  - `og:title/description/url/image/site_name/type` (`og:type` defaults to `website`)
  - `twitter:card` = `summary_large_image` with an image, else `summary`; plus `twitter:title/description/image`
- `truncateDescription()` cuts at 155 chars on a word boundary and strips any dangling space/comma/separator punctuation
- `escapeHtml()` escapes `& < > " '` in every attribute value
- `parseMeta(html)` uses cheerio to invert back to the object (title, description, canonical href, og/twitter fields)

**`/workspace/metagen/test/meta.test.js`** (Vitest)
1. Round-trip equality for fully populated and minimal canonical inputs (note: `type` is specified since `og:type` always renders with the `website` default)
2. Truncation of an exactly-200-char description: result ≤155, cut lands right before a whitespace in the original, no trailing comma/space; plus comma-at-boundary and short-circuit cases
3. Escaping: title containing `" < > & '` renders as entities and parses back exactly; `&` in the canonical URL is escaped too
4. Card switching: `summary_large_image` vs `summary`, with image tags appearing/disappearing accordingly

Run it anytime with `npx vitest run` from `/workspace/metagen`.
